metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >15% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.5) and price is trending up, model often overestimates — apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows after volatility spikes — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day avg, reduce by 5–10% for next 3 days.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often lags — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after a high forecast, model often fails to recognize “sell-off” sentiment — reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment turns negative within 2 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate downward trends — if true outcome shows 5%+ drop from 10-day avg, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often overfits recent data — use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast instead of 30-day trend.
